title: release check's declaration table has columns of a written width, and WP-08's assets.workflow key and release.verbs default overflow them, so their rows print the source out of line
body:
Found by vc on 2026-10-23, reading `bin/devbin release check` on main after the 0.1.13 batch landed (5460ac09).

`check_declaration` in lib/cmd/release prints each release key, its value, and whether it was declared or is the default, through `printf '  %-12s %-28s %s\n'`: columns of a width written into the code. ST0008 WP-08 added entries wider than those columns. The key `assets.workflow` is wider than the key column, and `verbs`' default value (`cut, status, notes, check, attach`) is wider than the value column, so on devbin's own declaration those two rows print their source out of line with every other row:

```
  object_wait  20m                          default
  after        bin/devbin formula publish   declared
  verbs        cut, status, notes, check, attach default
  assets.workflow (none)                       default
```

A project's own values overflow the same way: a long `repo`, a workflow path, or an `after:` command.

Fix: size each column from the longest entry it prints (the keys from `_DEVBIN_RELEASE_SCHEMA`, the values as read), so no width is written into the code. releasecore.bats:559 reads each row by its key at the line's start, which a computed width keeps; an arm holds every row's source at one column for a fixture whose key and value are both wider than any written today.

Cosmetic: every value printed is right. For the next batch release.


## Resolution

Fixed at c8d48d07, on landing suite 20261024-1756 at 62c632b4 (2474 of 2474 ok, 5 environmental skips, the errors seal empty), with the fleet-less candidate suite 20261024-1805 from the same tip (2319 of 2319 ok, 5 environmental skips, the errors seal empty). cc built it in a scratch clone, and vc landed it.

- check_declaration (lib/cmd/release) collects its rows first and sizes the key and value columns to the longest key and value this run prints, through `_release_widest` (lib/release.steps), which 0209's release_row uses for its columns too. No width is written in the code, so assets.workflow and release.verbs' default no longer push their source out of line.
- releasecore holds every row's source at one column for a declaration whose after: command and assets.workflow are wider than any value the old columns fitted. It was red on the base.
